title: Cohort Risk-Scoring and Cost-Aware Auto-Rollback Engine for Canary Traffic
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Implement an automated rollback trigger subsystem that computes a risk score per traffic cohort using multiple SLO signals (p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost per response, throughput) and applies dynamic thresholds that adapt to baseline variability. The goal is to reduce false positive rollbacks during transient noise while ensuring fast evacuation for real degradations, and to incorporate token-cost regressions into rollback decisions to protect unit economics. The system will integrate with the existing rollout controller, the Console UX, and runtime telemetry pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Risk score is computed for each cohort and exposed via telemetry (redisplayable as a single numeric signal)
Rollback decisions can be evaluated using risk score + configured sensitivity bands and executed by the rollout controller automatically
Dynamic thresholds adapt using a 7-day rolling baseline and decay windows to avoid punishing cold-start canaries
Token-cost delta (per-request token cost) is included as a first-class signal and can be weighted in policies
Console shows cohort risk and gives operators a one-click override (pause/rollback/hold) and a timeline of contributing signals
Automated rollback unit tests and integration tests simulate common failure modes (latency spike, spike in 5xxs, cost regression) and verify correct action within configured SLO windows
notes: Design choice: use additive risk scoring (normalized z-scores per metric) with configurable weights per signal; allows explainability in Console
We will bootstrap baselines from last 7 days of traffic and apply a minimum sample threshold before auto-evacuation (e.g., 500 requests per cohort per 5m window)
Include an option for ‘cost-aware mode’ where token-cost weight raises sensitivity for large customers with cost SLAs
Fallback behavior: if telemetry is degraded for >2 consecutive windows, halt auto-rollback and surface an alert to SRE
Plan to reuse existing rollout hooks (canary controller v2) and tracing spans to attribute errors to model variant and region
